title: Context Fabric Org document, contract 1
description: What one organization publishes about the systems it owns: what each system is, how to reach it, what it will not do, and who answers for it. The contract is the authority on what an Org document contains; prose describing it elsewhere is commentary.
$comment: This directory is released and immutable. A change of shape creates schemas/org/2/ with a migration step beside it.

allOf.$comment: Every string in the document, at any depth, carries the shared-tier prohibitions. Recursive rather than field-by-field so a field added later is covered without anybody remembering to cover it.

id.description: This document's identifier, stable across every move and rename. It is what a Bounded Context references, so changing it breaks references that changing a filename would not.

kind.description: Which contract this document is written against. It is what tells a reader which tier to check it under, so a near miss is a document nothing can classify.

schema_version.description: The contract version this document is written against.

release.description: This document's release number. A Bounded Context records the release it read, so this is what makes a stale reference visible instead of silent.

organization.description: The organization whose systems this document describes.

maintainer.description: Who answers for this document as a whole, when that differs from the organization's own maintainer.

secret_storage.description: Where this organization's practitioners keep the credentials its systems need. It names the store and how to get access to it, never a reference into it and never a value.

systems.description: The systems this organization owns. A system nobody here owns belongs in the organization that owns it, referenced rather than copied.

secret_store.title: Secret store
secret_store.description: A place credentials live. The entry exists so an Individual document can say which store it draws from; it carries no reference and no value.

guidance.description: How someone who needs access gets it.

id.description: The system's identifier, which a Bounded Context references as <document-id>#<system-id>.

name.description: What the organization calls the system.

kind.description: What kind of thing the system is. The list is what the framework knows how to say something useful about; something outside it is better described as a limitation than mislabelled.

status.description: Where the system sits in its life.

previous_ids.description: Identifiers this system has had before. A rename stays visible here, so a reference written against the old id is reported as renamed rather than missing.

interfaces.description: The ways into the system. An interface nobody can reach is still worth recording, with the reason in its limitations.

interface.title: Interface
interface.description: One way into a system: where it is, what it speaks, what it expects at the door, and what it will not do.

id.description: The interface's identifier, unique within its system.

status.description: Where the interface sits in its life.

previous_ids.description: Identifiers this interface has had before.

urls.description: Where the interface answers. HTTPS, or plain HTTP against loopback when the interface runs on the practitioner's own machine.

network.description: Which network the interface is reachable from, which is often the whole answer to why somebody cannot reach it.

auth.description: What the interface expects at the door.

access_check.description: A request a practitioner can make to prove they have access, and what a working answer looks like.

limitations.description: What this interface will not do, in the reader's terms. An empty list is a claim -- that somebody looked and found none -- which is why the key is required and its absence is not the same as an empty list.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.description: How a caller proves who it is, and which environment variables carry the answer. The variable's purpose is recorded here; where its value comes from is an Individual document's business.

method.description: How the interface authenticates a caller. host-tool means a tool already signed in on the machine -- a forge CLI, a cloud SDK -- carries the credential, so the interface needs no variable of its own.

env.description: Each environment variable the interface expects, and what it is for. Never a value, and never a reference to one: this tier is shared.

renamed_env.description: Variables this interface used to expect under another name, as previous name -> current name. It exists so a practitioner who bound the previous name is told it was RENAMED rather than that it is missing, and so reconciliation can re-point the binding instead of leaving it for them to guess at. The current name belongs in env.

access_check.title: Access check
access_check.description: The cheapest request that distinguishes having access from not having it.

expect.description: What a working answer looks like.
